headline: Yields rebound to 5% and steady the dollar; Brent near $117 sends the peso to another record low
summary: The dollar index rose about 0.15% to near 101.75, ending the week roughly flat, as 10-year Treasury yields rebounded about 5bp to 5.00% after Thursday's plunge and US flash PMIs showed manufacturing at a 53-month high with the fastest price rises in four years. The Aussie and loonie led on a broad bid for commodity currencies, while the franc gave back Thursday's haven gains, the euro hit a one-year low on the yen after a weak euro-area PMI, and the peso set a fifth straight record low as Brent spiked toward $117 on Trump's Iran threat.
drivers: Yields rebound after the AI scare

The 10-year Treasury yield climbed back to about 5.00% after Thursday's 17–19bp drop, and US flash PMIs held near five-year highs (composite 57.6, manufacturing 56.0 vs 55.6 expected) with selling prices up the most since 2022. That lifted the dollar index to about 101.75 from a three-week low of 101.45 and pushed USD/CHF up about 0.55% to 0.8249.

Brent hit about $117, the highest since May, and WTI rose about 4% to near $103.5 after Trump told a rally the US may do 'another little Epic Fury' against Iran and Houthi attacks on Saudi sites continued. The peso fell to a record 63.615 and the rupee to 94.93, while oil and a report that Washington may lift some 50% tariffs helped the loonie to a five-week high at 1.3969.
Weak euro-area PMI adds to France

The euro-area composite PMI fell to 51.9, a four-month low, against 52.7 expected, with France back in contraction as protests and a 2011-level bond spread weigh. EUR/USD slipped about 0.1% to near 1.1203 and EUR/JPY touched 175.08, its lowest since October 2025.
view: Range-bound to mildly weaker against the yen and Canadian dollar over the next 1–2 weeks: US data are strong, but the Fed is expected to hold next week, yields are about 35bp off their highs and AI-led equity stress keeps a haven bid in the yen. I fade the dollar against the yen and loonie, but back it against the euro on French stress and against the peso and rupiah while Brent sits above $110, with US strikes on Iran a live weekend risk. A hawkish Fed on Oct 28 that firmly signals December, or a DXY close above 102.30, would turn me dollar-positive; a break below 101.30 opens 101.
ideas: Sell rallies into 157.50–157.80 as Japan's 2.4% core-core CPI keeps a December BoJ hike in play, for 155.00, stop 158.60, about 2.5:1.
New short: sell 1.1240–1.1260 after the PMI miss and French stress, for 1.1120, stop 1.1310, about 2:1.
Sell bounces into 1.4030–1.4050 on BoC hike bets, oil and tariff-relief hopes, for 1.3880, stop 1.4130, about 1.8:1.
review: USD/CHF's sell zone filled near 0.8250 and is flat, USD/IDR's long from 18,000 is about 0.3% in favour and USD/TWD's fade is flat with Taipei shut, while the USD/JPY, USD/CAD, USD/CNH, USD/KRW and EUR/JPY entries were not reached; every range held, and I turn EUR/USD lower on the PMI miss, USD/PHP higher on oil, move USD/SGD to a range after soft CPI and lower the CAD sell zone.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.1% to near 1.1203 after a weak euro-area PMI; failed again at 1.1240–1.1250.

view.call: Sell 1.1240–1.1260; PMI miss, France at 2011 spreads.

eurusd.why: Euro weakness did the moving. The euro-area flash composite PMI fell to 51.9 from 53.1 against 52.7 expected, its lowest in four months, with France back in contraction as protests continue and the French–German spread sits at its widest since 2011. A rebound in the 10-year Treasury yield to about 5% removed Thursday's support from lower US yields, leaving the pair near 1.1203.
eurusd.outlook: I turn bearish: sell 1.1240–1.1250 resistance for 1.1120 while French stress and a softer PMI trim ECB hike pricing. A close above 1.1310 would end the call; a calm French weekend or a hawkish ECB on Oct 29 are the risks.
eurusd.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), ECB (Oct 29), French spreads and protests, and euro-area flash CPI (Oct 30).

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.2% to near 1.3371; a strong PMI was offset by weak retail sales.

view.call: 1.3300–1.3450; buy dips, the Oct 28 Budget caps it.

gbpusd.why: Mixed UK data and a firmer dollar. The flash composite PMI rose to 53.1, an eight-month high, against 51.8 expected, but September retail sales fell 0.4% against a 0.1% drop forecast, and a November BoE hike is already almost fully priced. With the dollar bouncing after four days of losses and the 10-year Treasury back at 5%, sterling eased from Thursday's highs near 1.3400.
gbpusd.outlook: Still a 1.3300–1.3450 range bought from the bottom: BoE hike pricing supports sterling, but the Oct 28 Budget caps it. A daily close above 1.3450 turns me bullish; a gilt selloff after the Budget is the risk.
gbpusd.watch: The Budget and the Fed (Oct 28), and the BoE (Nov 5).

audusd.note: Up about 0.2% to near 0.7033, leading the majors, but stalled at the 100-day average.
audusd.why: The Aussie led on the commodity bid despite weak local data. Australia's flash composite PMI fell to 47.7 from 51.3, the first contraction in five months, but prices rose and markets still see a good chance of a Nov 3 RBA hike. A firmer yuan and a calmer equity session after Thursday's rout lifted it toward the 100-day moving average, where sellers appeared.
audusd.outlook: Range 0.6950–0.7080: RBA hike bets support dips, while the AI selloff and the 100-day average cap rallies. Australia's September CPI (Oct 28) decides the break; a close above 0.7080 would turn me bullish.
audusd.watch: Australia CPI (Oct 28), yuan fixings, risk sentiment and the RBA on Nov 3.

usdjpy.note: Flat near 156.81 after dipping to 156.25 on Japan's CPI; the yen had its best week since early September.

view.call: Sell rallies 157.50–157.80; CPI backs BoJ, haven bid.

usdjpy.why: Two forces cancelled out. Japan's core CPI rose 2.1% and the BoJ's preferred core-core measure 2.4%, above forecasts, which keeps a December hike in play and pushed the pair to about 156.25. But the rebound in the 10-year Treasury yield to about 5% and a strong US manufacturing PMI lifted it back toward 157, where large option expiries sat, for a close near 156.81.
usdjpy.outlook: I keep selling rallies into 157.50–157.80 for 155.00: the rate gap is narrowing, BoJ hike odds for December are high and Iran escalation would add to haven demand. A close above 158.60, over the 200-day average, would end the call.
usdjpy.watch: Iran headlines over the weekend, the Fed (Oct 28) and the BoJ (Oct 30), where an upgraded inflation forecast would help the yen.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.55% to near 0.8249, the weakest major, as Thursday's haven buying unwound.

view.call: Short from 0.8240–0.8260; haven bid, Iran risk.

usdchf.why: The franc did the moving as haven demand faded. With US stock futures steadier and the 10-year Treasury yield back near 5%, some of Thursday's flight into the franc reversed, and the pair climbed to the 0.8240–0.8245 area where the 100-hour average and option expiries sat. The franc still gained on the euro for the week as French spreads widened.
usdchf.outlook: My sell zone at 0.8240–0.8260 has filled; I hold for 0.8100 because the haven case is intact with Iran strikes a live risk. A close above 0.8330 would end the call.
usdchf.watch: Iran and Gulf headlines, European bond spreads and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdcad.note: Flat near 1.4001 after touching 1.3969, a five-week low, on oil and retail sales.

view.call: Sell bounces 1.4030–1.4050; BoC hike bets, oil.

usdcad.why: The loonie did the work. Canadian retail sales rose 1.2% in August with an early 0.7% estimate for September, backing bets on a Bank of Canada hike to 2.50% on Oct 28, and US crude settled about 3.8% higher near $103 as Iran tensions rose. A report that Washington may lift 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods added support, though firmer US yields pulled the pair back to about 1.40 by the close.
usdcad.outlook: Still short, but I lower the sell zone to 1.4030–1.4050 because bounces are shallow; target 1.3880, near the 200-day average. A close above 1.4130 would end the call; a dovish BoC hold is the main risk.
usdcad.watch: The BoC and Fed decisions (Oct 28), oil, Iran headlines and US–Canada tariff news.

usdcnh.note: Yuan steady near 6.669 offshore after the strongest PBOC fix since February 2023, at 6.7180.

view.call: Sell bounces toward 6.69; a slow grind at the PBOC's pace.

usdcnh.why: The PBOC kept guiding the yuan higher, but slowly: the 6.7180 midpoint was its strongest in over three and a half years yet 422 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate, a sign it wants a gradual climb. The yuan held near multi-year highs and was set for a fourth weekly gain, helped by a large trade surplus and exporters' conversion, while a firmer dollar elsewhere kept it from going further.
usdcnh.outlook: A managed grind lower; I still sell bounces toward 6.69 for 6.64. A fix set closer to estimates would speed the move; a close above 6.71 or a deeper China stock selloff would stop it.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings versus estimates, US–China headlines and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdhkd.note: Back up to about 7.842 from 7.836 as US yields rebounded and HIBOR kept sliding.
usdhkd.why: Rate spreads moved it. The 10-year Treasury yield bounced about 5bp to near 5%, while one-month HIBOR has fallen for days to about 2.68%, a one-month low, which makes the carry trade of selling Hong Kong dollars for dollars more attractive again. No HKMA action or local catalyst was reported.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in a 7.83–7.85 band. A return to 7.85 would force the HKMA to buy Hong Kong dollars and tighten liquidity; a further fall in US yields would keep it off the weak edge.
usdhkd.watch: US yields, HIBOR, HKMA action at 7.85 and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdsgd.note: Up about 0.1% to near 1.2779 after core CPI eased to 2.0%, below the 2.3% forecast.

view.call: 1.2720–1.2830; soft CPI trims MAS tightening bets.

usdsgd.why: Local data and a firmer dollar. Singapore's core inflation slowed to 2.0% in September from 2.2% against a 2.3% forecast, and headline to 2.2%, which reduces the chance the MAS tightens in January after it held on Oct 14. The rebound in US yields added to it, though the Singapore dollar still moves far less than its neighbours.
usdsgd.outlook: I move from a short to a 1.2720–1.2830 range: softer inflation removes the tightening tailwind, while the S$NEER stays on the strong side of its band. A close below 1.2720 would reopen downside.
usdsgd.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), Singapore's Q3 data and the broad dollar.

usdkrw.note: Won eased 0.4 to 1,324.6 at the Seoul close, holding near its two-year high as the Kospi steadied.

view.call: Sell rallies into 1,335–1,340; BoK sees won undervalued.

usdkrw.why: Little changed after a big run. The Kospi rebounded 0.3% after Thursday's 3.5% slide as investors bought chip stocks on the dip, which kept foreign selling in check, and the Bank of Korea's comment on Thursday that the won is still undervalued continued to support it. A firmer dollar and oil near $114 kept the won from making a new high.
usdkrw.outlook: The trend still favours the won, so I keep selling rallies into 1,335–1,340 for 1,315 rather than chase. A close above 1,352 would end the call; a fresh exodus from chip stocks is the risk.
usdkrw.watch: Korea's Q3 GDP, foreign flows in Seoul, Samsung and SK hynix results, and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdtwd.note: No Taipei trading: markets shut for Typhoon Champi; offshore quotes near 32.57.

view.call: Fade 32.50–32.65; export receipts, central bank caps it.

usdtwd.why: Taiwan's markets were closed on Friday as Typhoon Champi shut most of the island, and Monday is a holiday, so the last onshore close remains Thursday's 32.508. Offshore quotes drifted to about 32.57, reflecting foreign equity outflows earlier in the week and the chip-stock rout in Seoul and Tokyo.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep fading weakness from about 32.55: export receipts are large and the central bank has said it will act, though foreign selling slows the trade. Target 32.10; a close above 32.80 would stop it.
usdtwd.watch: Taipei reopens Oct 27; foreign Taiex flows, TSMC and US big-tech earnings, and central bank action.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit eased to 4.0835/0875 at the 6pm close from 4.0815/0850, in a 4.0813–4.0865 range.
usdmyr.why: Caution before the Fed dominated. The ringgit opened firmer as the dollar index eased overnight, but worries about AI-linked stocks and a wait for next week's FOMC statement left it slightly weaker against the dollar by the close. It firmed against the euro and pound but fell against the yen.
usdmyr.outlook: Range-bound around 4.07–4.10. Strong exports and Bank Negara support it, but it rarely moves far without the broad dollar.
usdmyr.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), oil prices and Bank Negara's Nov 5 meeting.

usdphp.note: Peso fell 9.5 centavos to a record-low close of 63.615, its fifth straight record.

view.call: Buy dips 63.40–63.50; oil swamps the BSP hike.

usdphp.why: Oil overwhelmed the BSP's hike. Brent rose toward $113–117 on Houthi attacks and Iran escalation talk, lifting the import bill and dollar demand, while the BSP's raised 2027 inflation forecast of 6% fed worries about domestic prices. The peso touched a new intraday low of 63.62 even though the 50bp hike to 5.50% lifted local yields, and Governor Remolona has said the BSP only smooths moves.
usdphp.outlook: I turn from range to long USD/PHP: buy dips toward 63.40–63.50 for 64.00 while Brent stays above $110. A close below 63.15, likely on an Iran deal and lower oil, would end the call.
usdphp.watch: Iran strike headlines, oil, BSP dollar sales and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdidr.note: Rupiah near 18,040 at the Jakarta close (Refinitiv); BI's JISDOR rate eased to 18,069.

view.call: Long from 18,000; add on dips to 17,950. MSCI risk, oil.

usdidr.why: Mixed signals and little net change. A softer dollar in Asian hours let the rupiah recover from about 18,080 to end near 18,040, but Bank Indonesia's reference rate still weakened to 18,069 from 18,047. Oil above $110, MSCI's plan to cut Indonesia's market status and BI's defence of its easing policy mix kept foreign investors cautious.
usdidr.outlook: I stay long the dollar from near 18,000, about 0.3% in favour, targeting 18,250 while the MSCI threat stands and oil is high. A credible fix for MSCI that pulls it below 17,850 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Foreign flows into Jakarta stocks, the government's MSCI response, oil and BI intervention.

usdinr.note: Rupee fell 12 paise to 94.93, a second loss, as Brent neared $114; flat for the week.
usdinr.why: Oil did the damage again. Brent hovered near $114, on course for a third weekly gain, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, which revived oil importers' dollar demand and offset relief from easing US rate-hike odds. The rupee opened firmer at 94.78 but hit 94.98 before settling at 94.93, and foreign selling of Indian stocks added pressure.
usdinr.outlook: Range 94.30–95.30: IPO inflows and the RBI's limits on oil companies' spot buying cap the dollar, but oil above $110 blocks a rupee rally. I wouldn't chase either side.
usdinr.watch: Iran headlines and oil, RBI action, foreign portfolio flows and the Fed on Oct 28.

eurjpy.note: Fell about 0.1% to near 175.67 after touching 175.08, the lowest since October 2025.

view.call: Sell rallies 176.50–177.00; France and haven yen.

eurjpy.why: The euro was the weak leg. A miss in the euro-area PMI and France's return to contraction weighed on the single currency, while Japan's firmer core-core CPI briefly boosted the yen, sending the cross to about 175.08. It recovered as US yields rose and USD/JPY bounced, closing near 175.67 (EUR/USD 1.1203 × USD/JPY 156.81), down about 1.2% for the week.
eurjpy.outlook: Bearish: sell rallies into 176.50–177.00 for 174.00 while France and the risk-off mood weigh. A close above 177.80 would end the call; a French de-escalation is the main risk.
eurjpy.watch: French spreads, the ECB (Oct 29) and BoJ (Oct 30), and risk sentiment.

cnhjpy.note: Flat near 23.51 as the yen and yuan both held their gains.
cnhjpy.why: Neither leg moved much. USD/JPY ended almost unchanged after a CPI-led dip, and the PBOC kept the yuan near multi-year highs with a fix at 6.7180, so the cross stayed near 23.51 (USD/JPY 156.81 divided by USD/CNH 6.669).
cnhjpy.outlook: No edge in a 23.3–23.8 range, sitting in the lower half. A break below 23.3 would need USD/JPY under about 155.5.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, the BoJ on Oct 30 and risk sentiment.

watch: Next: Taipei reopens and the Fed meets (Oct 27–28), the BoC, Australia CPI and UK Budget (Oct 28), the ECB (Oct 29) and BoJ (Oct 30), the RBA (Nov 3), US midterms (Nov 3), the BoE and Bank Negara (Nov 5), plus Iran strike headlines, oil and Tokyo's 159–160 line.
